next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework update found in Baba corpus; CFO on 2026-08-04: "We're probably not going to share kind of 2027" (document_id 128975). Next scheduled item is Q3 2026 earnings (date not confirmed).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Marqeta reports adjusted EBITDA margin on net revenue and also on gross profit (31% in Q2 2026). The only current number is a one-year FY2026 guide expressed as adjusted EBITDA growth (low 30s, raised from mid-20s) with net revenue growth 12-13%, which implies about 20.3% margin on net revenue. No long-term margin level, annual rate or dated target exists. The 2023 Investor Day 2025-26 frame (mid-single to low-double digit margins, per a search snippet of an analyst restating it, not verified) is already far exceeded.

statements.quote: Therefore, we expect full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA to grow in the mid-20s, more than twice our gross profit growth rate.
statements.speaker: Patti Kangwankij

statements.quote: We do feel like we will continue to have a decent spread between our gross profit growth and our expense growth. Our earnings growth will continue to exceed the top-line growth for some time.
statements.speaker: Mike Milotich

statements.quote: I'll start. We're probably not going to share kind of 2027.
statements.speaker: Patti Kangwankij

street.gap_assumption: No long-term target; compares the FY2026 guide-implied margin (FY2025 adj EBITDA $109.578M x 1.30 over FY2025 revenue $624.884M x 1.125, = 20.26%) with FY2026 consensus 20.59%. December fiscal year, so Baba FY labels equal company fiscal years.

evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026 adj EBITDA margin 20.1% vs 14.4% (+567 bps); Q2 2026 21.3% vs 19.0% (+231 bps), from 8-K 0001522540-26-000061. Expansion is opex discipline (Q2 adj opex +12%) while gross profit growth decelerates to 5-7% in Q3 on Block pricing tier, renewals and Cash App issuance diversification.

disqualifier_reason: Margin framing already reflected in consensus: the only numeric frame (FY2026 guide, implied about 20.3%) sits 33 bps below FY2026 consensus 20.6%, and consensus already models 22.0% FY2027 and 23.8% FY2028 with no management number above it. The debate is gross profit deceleration and Block concentration, not an unmodeled margin story.
verdict: Cheap and leadership is refreshed (internal CEO, external CFO, CTO, CPO), but there is no margin target and consensus already sits above guidance.
open_questions: Will the new CFO give a 2027 or multi-year framework, or keep to annual guides?
How much of 2026 margin expansion is opex timing (back-loaded 2025 spend) versus durable operating leverage?
Does gross profit growth re-accelerate in 2027 once Block tiering and the last renewals lap?
